# CS 29.45 — General (performance)

> [!summary]
> CS 29.45 fixes the conditions under which large rotorcraft performance is
> determined. It is a CS-29 specification, not a CS-E one, and the rotorcraft
> applicant owns it. Performance is determined with normal piloting skill and
> without exceptionally favourable conditions. It is shown for still air at sea
> level and across the approved range of atmospheric variables, at a prescribed
> relative humidity. Available power is engine power less installation and
> accessory losses. A pre-take-off power check is required.

## Requirement

The verbs below are CS-29's own. They bind the rotorcraft applicant, not the
engine applicant. See `## Bearing on this engine` for what reaches CS-E.

| Ref | Obligation | Strength |
|---|---|---|
| **(a)** | Determine the performance prescribed in this subpart under the two conditions of (a)(1) and (a)(2). | Required |
| **(a)(1)** | Determine it with normal piloting skill. | Required |
| **(a)(2)** | Determine it without exceptionally favourable conditions. | Required |
| **(b)** | Show compliance with the performance requirements of this subpart in the two cases of (b)(1) and (b)(2). | Required |
| **(b)(1)** | Show it for still air at sea-level with a standard atmosphere. | Required |
| **(b)(2)** | Show it for the approved range of atmospheric variables. | Required |
| **(c)** | Take the available power as engine power, not exceeding the approved power, less the two deductions of (c)(1) and (c)(2). | Required |
| **(c)(1)** | Deduct installation losses. | Required |
| **(c)(2)** | Deduct the power absorbed by the accessories and services at the values for which certification is requested and approved. | Required |
| **(d)** | For reciprocating engine-powered rotorcraft, base the performance, as affected by engine power, on a relative humidity of 80% in a standard atmosphere. | Required |
| **(e)** | For turbine engine-powered rotorcraft, base the performance, as affected by engine power, on the relative humidity of (e)(1) and (e)(2). | Required |
| **(e)(1)** | The value at and below standard temperature is 80%. | Statement |
| **(e)(2)** | The value at and above standard temperature plus 28°C (50°F) is 34%. | Statement |
| **(e)** | Between these two temperatures, vary the relative humidity linearly. | Required |
| **(f)** | For turbine-engine-powered rotorcraft, provide a means to permit the pilot to determine prior to take-off that each engine is capable of developing the power necessary to achieve the applicable rotorcraft performance prescribed in this subpart. | Required |

Sub-point (a) has no CS-27 counterpart. CS-29 fixes how the performance is
determined: with normal piloting skill, and "Without exceptionally favourable
conditions" [ext CS 29.45(a)(2)]. CS 27.45 carries no such clause.

The two codes set the atmosphere differently, and the difference is
substantive. CS-29 asks for compliance "For still air at sea-level with a
standard atmosphere" and, as a separate case, "For the approved range of
atmospheric variables" [ext CS 29.45(b)]. CS-27 asks only that the requirements
of its Subpart "must be met for still air and a standard atmosphere"
[ext CS 27.45(a)]. It names no sea-level datum and no approved range. CS-27
instead carries a sub-point (b) that CS-29 has no counterpart to, tying the
performance to "the engine power available under the particular ambient
atmospheric conditions, the particular flight condition, and the relative
humidity specified in sub-paragraphs (d) or (e), as appropriate"
[ext CS 27.45(b)]. The two codes reach the ambient frame from opposite ends.

Sub-point (c) differs in its second deduction only. CS-29 takes the accessory
and services power "at the values for which certification is requested and
approved" [ext CS 29.45(c)(2)]. CS-27 takes it "appropriate to the particular
ambient atmospheric conditions and the particular flight condition"
[ext CS 27.45(c)(2)]. CS-29 fixes one approved set of values; CS-27 varies the
set with the condition. The opening words of (c) are identical in both codes.

Sub-points (d), (e) and (f) are the same in substance in both codes. Both carry
80% at and below standard temperature and 34% at and above standard temperature
plus 28°C (50°F), and both vary the humidity linearly between those two
temperatures. In the CS-27 text the linear-variation sentence runs on from
(e)(2); in CS-29 it stands as a separate sentence after it. The values and the
rule are the same. Sub-point (f) differs only in the hyphenation of
"turbine-engine-powered" and in the capitalisation of Subpart.

## Bearing on this engine

CS 29.45 creates no CS-E obligation. It binds the rotorcraft applicant, who
determines the performance of the installed aircraft. What the point does is
consume engine data, and CS-E names that data in three places.

**Approved power.** Sub-point (c) caps the available power at engine power "not
exceeding the approved power" [ext CS 29.45(c)]. Those are the ratings
established under [[CS-E 40]] and listed in the type certificate data sheet
[CS-E 40(e)]. This engine declares Take-off Power and Maximum Continuous Power
[CS-E 40(a)], Rated 30-Minute Power [CS-E 40(b)(4)] and three OEI ratings
[CS-E 40(b)(3)].

**The basis of the declared power.** CS-E declares the ratings on standard
atmospheric conditions, with no air bleed for aircraft services and with only
the accessories essential for engine functioning installed [CS-E 40(c)]. Any
other basis is declared in the type certificate data sheet [CS-E 40(c)].
Sub-point (c) of CS 29.45 starts from that figure and subtracts installation
losses [ext CS 29.45(c)(1)] and accessory and services power
[ext CS 29.45(c)(2)]. The engine-level half of that subtraction reaches the
installer as the installation losses definable at engine level of
[[AMC E 20|AMC E 20(f)(1)]].

**Ambient conditions and humidity.** Sub-point (b)(2) extends compliance to the
approved range of atmospheric variables, and (e) fixes the humidity the engine
power is read at. [[CS-E 20|CS-E 20(e)]] is the engine-side supply for both: the
engine performance data must include means of determining the effect on
performance of engine bleed, power off-take, forward speed, ambient pressure,
temperature and humidity [CS-E 20(e)]. The range itself is an assumption about
the installation. It is submitted before engine certification and carried in the
instructions for installation under [[CS-E 30|CS-E 30(a)]], and the operating
limitations for the intended operating conditions are established under
[CS-E 40(d)].

**Power assurance.** Sub-point (f) is the pre-take-off power check. CS-E answers
it directly: for an engine having one or more OEI ratings, the applicant
provides data on engine performance characteristics and variability so that the
aircraft manufacturer can establish power assurance procedures [CS-E 20(f)].
The scope of that data is set by [[AMC E 20|AMC E 20(f)(1)]], which names this
sub-point as the specification the data serves [AMC E 20(f)(1)]. This engine
declares three OEI ratings, so [[CS-E 20|CS-E 20(f)]] binds.

[VERIFY: which engine parameters the power assurance means reads. Neither
CS 29.45(f) nor CS-E 20(f) names one. Provision for engine instrumentation is a
separate CS-E obligation [CS-E 60(a)], and the list of instruments necessary for
control of the engine reaches the installer under [CS-E 60(b)]; whether the
power assurance means needs anything beyond that list is an installation
question.]

**What does not reach this engine.** Sub-point (d) is for reciprocating
engine-powered rotorcraft and has no bearing on a turboshaft [ext CS 29.45(d)].
Sub-point (a) governs piloting technique and test conditions, and asks nothing
of the engine [ext CS 29.45(a)].

[VERIFY: whether the installation is certificated under CS-29 or CS-27. The
counterpart point [[CS 27.45]] sets the atmospheric frame differently and
qualifies the accessory deduction differently. [[CS-E 30]] carries the same open
item.]
